title: bug: VS Code prior-handoff card reads from/to/createdAt, but the daemon writes releasedBy/releasedAt/reason, so every card title is just "#N" (VS Code twin of the DONE JetBrains fix ac587df5)
definitionOfDone: VS Code's HandoffNote type and renderHandoff use releasedBy, releasedAt and reason. The card title matches the JetBrains header (d5f36e82): "#N released by X (time): reason", each part only when present and HTML-escaped. A note without them still renders "#N".

The task-time-budget fixture uses the daemon's handoff shape, and a test fails if the title reads from/to/createdAt again. moe-vscode `npm test` and `npm run compile` pass. No file outside moe-vscode/ changes.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix the type and the title in moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts, moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts and moe-vscode/CHANGELOG.md.
(a) moe.ts HandoffNote (line 202): replace from?/to?/createdAt? with `releasedBy?: string; releasedAt?: string; reason?: string;` and keep the four body fields. Add a one-line doc comment naming HandoffNote in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts. With the old keys gone, `npm run compile` fails if anything reads them again. Do not add diskState: it is not shown, and JetBrains omits it too.
(b) TaskDetailPanel.ts renderHandoff (line 1310): build the title as `#${index}` + part(' released by ', h.releasedBy) + part(' (', h.releasedAt, ')') + part(': ', h.reason). Use a nested helper `const part = (prefix: string, value: unknown, suffix = ''): string => typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() ? prefix + escapeHtml(value) + suffix : '';`. These are exactly the JetBrains header strings (TaskDetailDialog.kt handoffBlocks, d5f36e82), with ONE space before '(' where the old VS Code code had two. Note the parity in a 2-line comment above the function. Leave block() and the card body untouched.
Error handling: renderHandoff runs inside the panel's HTML build, so a throw there would blank the whole Task Detail panel. The typeof guard therefore treats null, arrays, objects, numbers and blank strings as absent and never calls .trim() on a non-string. release_task only ever writes strings (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/releaseTask.ts), so the guard only matters for hand-edited or corrupt .moe state.
(c) CHANGELOG.md: append one bullet at the end of [Unreleased] → ### Fixed (the card shipped in 0.8.0): '- Each **Prior hand-offs** card in task detail is titled with who released the task, when and why (`#1 released by <worker> (<time>): <reason>`), as in JetBrains. Before, the title was only `#1`, `#2` and so on.'
Then re-run step 1's quick command: 12/12 ok. Reference bytes: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-5a5a7189/fix.diff (git apply --check passes against 6029cee3); copy with Edit.

Verification gate. From the task worktree root, run the first executionContract checkRef verbatim. The same text is saved as /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-5a5a7189/checkref-gate.txt (sha256 a11c4a9828eec18b4df1a29d6ca650403e1d7e89f1eb645958fa31c064ff49a1).
What it does: it snapshots the worktree's HEAD plus the three edited source/test files into a fresh /tmp/m5a5.* dir. That is needed because a worktree has no node_modules, the rail forbids npm ci inside the repo tree, and the shared node_modules hold only win32 tsc (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl, mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot). There it runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run compile` under a clean env with nvm node v24.21.0. Then it swaps in the merge-base TaskDetailPanel.ts and requires exactly two failing rows, both naming 'handoff': a RED re-proof that the tests catch a from/to/createdAt reader (mem:convention-vscode-port-mutant-checkref).
Planner dry run at 430e4620: exit 0; ℹ tests 696, pass 686, fail 0, skipped 10 (Windows-only rows); RED: not ok 10 and not ok 11. Counts may shift by rows that other landings add. Its fresh output is the complete_task verification evidence.
Error handling for a red run: if npm ci, the tests or compile fail, the command prints the snapshot path and its last 40 log lines and exits 1. Fix the code and rerun. A RED count other than 2 means a test was renamed or is vacuous: fix the test, never the command.
Never run npm ci or npm install in the worktree or the shared checkout. Afterwards delete the /tmp/m5a5.* dir your run created, by its literal path.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: VS Code Task Detail 'Prior hand-offs' card titles read the daemon's HandoffNote fields and match the JetBrains header from d5f36e82: '#N', then ' released by <releasedBy>', then ' (<releasedAt>)', then ': <reason>'. Each part appears only when its field is a non-blank string, and every value is HTML-escaped. A note with none of them, including a legacy from/to/createdAt-only note, is titled '#N'. Malformed values (null, arrays, objects) never throw.
acceptanceCriteria: A note {releasedBy:'w', releasedAt:'t', reason:'r'} at position 1 renders the card title '#1 released by w (t): r'.
Each part appears only when its field is a non-blank string. A note without any of them (including from/to/createdAt only) renders '#N', and null/array/object values render '#N' without throwing.
Every interpolated value goes through the panel's escapeHtml, for example worker-<a> renders as worker-<a>.
moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts HandoffNote declares releasedBy/releasedAt/reason and no longer declares from/to/createdAt.
The task-time-budget richTask fixture uses the daemon's handoff shape. Against the merge-base renderer, exactly the two handoff rows fail.
moe-vscode npm test and npm run compile pass in a Linux snapshot of the worktree, and no file outside moe-vscode/ changes.
invariants: Every value interpolated into the card title passes escapeHtml.
The card body sections (What is done, What remains, Pitfalls, Open questions) render exactly as before.
compatibility: No daemon, wire, JetBrains or .moe/ change. The daemon already writes releasedBy/releasedAt/reason (releaseTask.ts), so existing notes start showing their header as soon as the fix lands.
A legacy note carrying only from/to/createdAt (a shape the daemon never wrote) renders '#N' and never throws.
The board.js hand-off chip reads only priorHandoffs.length and is unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Keep from/to/createdAt as fallbacks for old notes. Rejected: the daemon never wrote those keys, and JetBrains dropped them in d5f36e82. (b) Coerce JSON primitives the way JetBrains MoeJson.getStringOrNull does. Rejected: release_task writes only strings, and the typeof guard is enough to never throw. One accepted divergence: a number or boolean value is dropped in VS Code, while JetBrains would print it. (c) A new test file. Rejected: task-time-budget.test.cjs already owns the real-renderer harness and the fixture the DoD names. (d) A Windows leg in the gate. Not needed: this is pure string rendering with no platform branch, and the Linux snapshot runs the full suite plus compile.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The tests transpile the real TaskDetailPanel.ts into node:vm and read webview.html (mem:convention-vscode-renderer-tests). The panel imports HandoffNote type-only, so the compile leg is what proves nothing else reads the removed fields. board.js only counts priorHandoffs for its chip. A fresh task worktree has no node_modules: the gate snapshots into /tmp and runs npm ci there, and a quick run uses NODE_PATH into the control checkout's moe-vscode/node_modules (TS6 JS, which works under WSL). The planner dry-ran the full fix and both checkRefs. The reference diff, the check texts and the dry-run output are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-5a5a7189/.
planningNotes.risks: 1) Use the new test's name exactly and keep the existing test's name. The gate's RED leg needs exactly 2 failing rows that both contain 'handoff'. 2) One space before '(' (JetBrains), not the old two. 3) Never run npm ci or npm install in the worktree or the shared checkout (rail). 4) For QA: re-run checkRef 1 at the control checkout with MOE_LAND_TARGET=<completion>^, so the merge-base is the pre-fix parent. Check scope with `git diff --name-only <completion>^ <completion>`: the control checkout's daemon-written .moe/ diffs would trip checkRef 2 there.
